children: Our Bureau Mumbai: The 30,213-crore initial public offering (IPO) of Jio Platforms, the largest in Indian corporate history, was subscribed 3.16 times on Wednesday. The issue was fully subscribed within 100 minutes, driven by strong demand from institutional investors.

The IPO will remain open until Friday. Investors placed bids for 623.6 million shares against 197.5 million shares on offer, with the bids valued at 69,800 crore at the upper end of the price band, according to combined data from both stock exchanges as of 7 pm on Wednesday. The IPO is priced at 1,065-1,119 per share. The qualified institutional buyers' (QIB) portion was subscribed 9.42 times, with bids for 461.5 million shares against 49 million shares reserved for the category.

The non-institutional investors' (NII) portion was subscribed 1.68 times, receiving bids for 61.2 million shares against 36.4 million shares on offer. The retail portion was subscribed 0.73 times, with bids for 61.7 million shares against 85 million shares reserved for the category. The employee quota was subscribed 1.36 times, while the shareholder portion was subscribed 1.46 times.

title: GONE in 100 Minutes Jio IPO Bids Hit 70kcr on Day 1
